Theorem
[Curvature blows up at a singularity] Source: topping:page-0064, topping:page-0065, topping:page-0066, topping:page-0067 ↗ topping-maxpr-curvature-norm-bound ↗ topping-maxpr-higher-derivatives ↗ topping-ricci-flow-metric-equivalence 1. ch5:3.1\group topping-ricci-flow-existence

If $\M $ is closed and $g(t)$ is a Ricci flow on a maximal interval $[0,T)$ with $T<\infty $, then \[ \sup _{\M }|\Rm |(\cdot ,t)\longrightarrow \infty \qquad ext{as }t\uparrow T. \]

Proof

\sketch If $|\Rm |$ were bounded on $[0,T)$, Theorem topping-maxpr-curvature-norm-bound would give a uniform bound $|\Rm |\leq M$ on $\M imes [0,T)$. The Ricci bound and the metric-equivalence lemma would then imply that $g(t)$ converges continuously to a positive-definite tensor $g(T)$ as $t\uparrow T$.

On $[ rac12T,T)$, Corollary topping-maxpr-higher-derivatives bounds all quantities $\partial _t^\ell abla ^k\Rm $. Together with the Ricci-flow equation and the commutator formula for $\partial _t$ and $ abla $, these bounds control all mixed space-time derivatives of the coordinate coefficients $g_{ij}$. Hence $g(t)$ extends smoothly to $T$. Applying the short-time existence theorem to $g(T)$ extends the flow beyond $T$, contradicting maximality.

□
